statusDetail: Coverage-complete report-mode audit. The mandatory age gate limited visual access to post-confirmation states, but rendered DOM and direct route responses remained inspectable and every registered check received a conclusive outcome.

page.notes: Public Russian-language media/listing site with a mandatory age gate, cookie consent, advertising, a detail template, search, and account entry points.

paths.description: Homepage/listing and mandatory age/consent entry state. Represents the primary discovery surface.
Section/listing archetype requested directly. It redirected to home before retaining the requested path.
Representative media detail template, including player, metadata, channel links, and report form.
Primary account-entry journey requested directly. It redirected to home before exposing the form.
Recovery-state test using an unknown URL. The server returned a 200 homepage instead of a 404.

findings.summary: The palette is hard-coded rather than preference-driven.
findings.evidence: The default and dark-condition screenshots are byte-identical at 63,768 bytes, and recon found no preference-driven theming. The fixed dark palette is usable but is not driven by the user preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and map surfaces through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() so browser UI and page colors follow the system preference.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion does not suppress non-essential transitions.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe confirmed the preference was active but still found 0.5s transitions on .scrollableBannerContent and #toastMessage, with no reduced-motion override.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override that removes non-essential transitions and auto-motion while preserving necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no directional transition cues.
findings.evidence: Recon found no view-transition CSS or API use; route probes show full-document navigation and abrupt age-gate redirects.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful route and state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long listings provide no scroll-position feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is a long listing, but recon found no scroll-state query, progress marker, or position-aware navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress affordance so navigation responds to long-page position.

findings.summary: Redirected navigation does not explain the resulting location.
findings.evidence: Categories, login, and unknown paths redirect to the homepage without a transition, route-specific heading, or focus cue explaining where attention moved.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the requested destination through age verification and move focus to a route-specific heading or status message after navigation.

findings.summary: Multiple first-load notices compete before content.
findings.evidence: First load stacks a full-screen age gate with a separate three-choice cookie prompt in the accessibility tree before the primary content. The legal gate is expected, but the layered interruption increases first-use friction.
findings.suggestedFix: Combine or sequence mandatory notices, keep essential-cookie continuation prominent, and avoid presenting multiple interruptive layers simultaneously.

findings.summary: Custom div overlays replace native dismissible primitives.
findings.evidence: Recon found 0 dialog, 0 popover, and 0 details elements even though the age gate is a custom div with role=alertdialog and cookie customization is custom div-based UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for the modal age flow and details or popover for expandable cookie controls, with native focus trapping, Escape behavior, and light dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Advertising chrome crowds the content experience.
findings.evidence: The listing contains repeated advertising placements and 31 TrafficJunky requests; the probe exposed many repeated “remove ads” controls, so non-content chrome competes heavily with the listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated ad chrome, reserve fewer placements, and defer non-essential below-fold ad UI until it is near the viewport.

findings.summary: The mandatory age gate is visibly clipped on a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: Although the layout metric reports no document-level horizontal overflow, the 360px screenshot visibly clips the logo, heading, legal copy, and the two age buttons off the right edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove fixed/min widths from the age-gate content and buttons, allow wrapping, and size the modal with min(100% - padding, max-width).

findings.summary: Reusable components depend on viewport assumptions rather than their container.
findings.evidence: Recon found no container-query CSS, and the reused age-gate component fails to adapt within the narrow viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and gate controls a containment context and use container queries or intrinsic grid/flex wrapping for narrow placements.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is often invisible and many targets are too short.
findings.evidence: Cookie buttons and search input computed to outline:none/0px when focused, many links measured 15 to 22px high, and the first 30 controls included many navigation links without a visible focus outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a clear :focus-visible ring with adequate contrast and provide at least 24px minimum, preferably 44px, target geometry for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Age-gate routing loses requested listing and sign-in destinations.
findings.evidence: The categories and /login requests both end at the homepage, while only the query-based detail route retains its URL. The requested flow context is lost before the user can continue through the age gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve the requested return URL through age verification and route users back to categories or sign-in after successful confirmation.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs silently become the homepage.
findings.evidence: An unknown path returns a 200 homepage with no not-found state, explanation, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an actual 404 response with a concise not-found message, search, and links back to useful destinations.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is well outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 16.8s, FCP 3.0s, and TBT about 80ms; the independent trace measured LCP 4.55s. Both LCP observations exceed the 2.5s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the actual LCP element, preload or prioritize it, reduce first-load ad and analytics work, and validate LCP under repeatable mobile conditions.

findings.summary: The mobile first load shifts after rendering.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive recorded CLS 0.1021 from a shift around 1.2s, just outside the good threshold; three images also lack explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for all images and late banners, and stabilize the gate layout before first paint.

findings.summary: A large blocking network graph delays primary rendering.
findings.evidence: The page made 172 requests and transferred 5.41MB. The HAR lists seven parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets and three high-priority parser scripts as blocking candidates; Lighthouse also failed LCP discovery and dependency-tree insights.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles and scripts, shorten dependency chains, and explicitly prioritize the LCP resource.

findings.summary: The first load ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 288KiB unused JavaScript and 74KiB unused CSS; three Google tag scripts account for much of the unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Load analytics once and only after consent, split route-specific code and styles, and remove duplicated or unused mobile bundles.

findings.summary: Several controls and frames lack reliable accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found multiple visible ad iframes without titles and a visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch on the header user button. The search input also has no associated label.
findings.suggestedFix: Title meaningful iframes, make visible and accessible control names match, and associate a persistent label or aria-label with search.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and page structure are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found outline:none on cookie actions and search and many navigation links without a visible outline; the age heading is H3 with no visible H1 on home.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a logical H1-led heading structure and a consistent :focus-visible style on every interactive element without removing the browser outline unless replaced.

findings.summary: Mandatory text is not fully legible on narrow screens.
findings.evidence: The mobile age-gate copy and heading are clipped off the right edge, preventing complete reading of the mandatory notice.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a fluid text container, balanced wrapping, and responsive font sizing so all mandatory copy remains inside the viewport.

findings.summary: Zoom is disabled and narrow reflow and target sizing are inadequate.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no/maximum-scale=1 on the mobile document, the screenshot fails reflow, and many interactive targets are only 15 to 22px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user zoom, fix narrow reflow, enlarge touch targets, and ensure video captions or equivalents are exposed on detail pages.

findings.summary: The homepage throws an uncaught JavaScript exception.
findings.evidence: A TypeError occurs in setInstallButton when addEventListener is called on null.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the queried install element before binding, initialize only when the control exists, and add a regression test for the first-load path.

findings.summary: Asset sizing and deprecated media styling weaken document hygiene.
findings.evidence: The document has a valid doctype and UTF-8 charset, but 3 images lack dimensions and Lighthouse reports deprecated media-control CSS usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width and height to images and replace deprecated internal media-control selectors with supported attributes and controls.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and avoidable BFCache blockers remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports deprecated unload listeners, inspector issues, and four BFCache failure reasons including the unload handler and cache-control:no-store.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers in favor of pagehide/visibilitychange, address DevTools issues, and use no-store only where sensitive responses require it.

findings.summary: Public pages lack unique descriptive titles and descriptions.
findings.evidence: All tested paths use the generic title “Pornhub” and no meta description, including the detail page with a specific H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit a unique title and concise description for each index and detail template.

findings.summary: Crawler directives and links prevent reliable discovery.
findings.evidence: The page declares noindex,nofollow, Lighthouse found javascript:void(0) anchors, and /robots.txt returns the full HTML page rather than valid robots directives.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid robots.txt, use real href destinations for content links, and remove nofollow/noindex when this public locale is intended to be indexed.

findings.summary: Canonical, status, robots, and sitemap signals conflict.
findings.evidence: The detail page canonical points to the homepage, listing and unknown paths redirect to the homepage with 200, every page is noindex, and /sitemap.xml returns 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Use self-referential canonicals on indexable templates, return correct HTTP statuses, align robots with intent, and publish a valid sitemap.

findings.summary: Video detail pages lack structured and share-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: Recon found no JSON-LD and no Open Graph metadata; the detail route exposes a rich video entity only in visible DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate VideoObject JSON-LD and Open Graph metadata derived from the visible detail content.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but key browser defenses and one cookie flag are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present and no client secrets were detected, but CSP and X-Content-Type-Options are missing and cookie rp is not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce- or hash-based CSP, add nosniff, and mark every HTTPS cookie Secure with an appropriate SameSite value.

findings.summary: A large tracking footprint loads before the user resolves consent.
findings.evidence: Before consent resolution, the load contacted 12 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and DoubleClick; 101 third-party requests transferred 2.26MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential analytics and advertising until explicit consent, minimize vendors and events, and batch the remaining measurement.

findings.summary: The response omits several browser-enforced defenses.
findings.evidence: CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and nosniff are missing; seven cookies use SameSite=None and rp is not Secure. HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrictive CSP/frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; reduce SameSite=None to only cookies that truly need cross-site use.

findings.summary: Core server HTML only partially represents the rendered page.
findings.evidence: The server sends substantial HTML and is not a JS shell, but only 45% of rendered content words overlap raw HTML and no H1 survives as a crawler-visible heading.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary listing and headings consistently, then layer personalization and ads on as enhancements.

findings.summary: Mandatory UI and initialization fail under realistic states.
findings.evidence: The age gate clips on a narrow viewport and the homepage throws while binding an install button, showing that layout and initialization are not robust to the current state.
findings.suggestedFix: Make gate layout intrinsic and guard optional runtime dependencies so missing elements do not break initialization.

findings.summary: HTTP failure states are replaced by misleading success.
findings.evidence: The unknown route silently returns a 200 homepage with no error explanation, retry, search, or preserved path.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a truthful status and a dedicated recovery state with search and navigation options.

findings.summary: Language is mixed and layout styling is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The document correctly uses lang=ru, but the probe found 0 logical-property tokens versus 181 physical left/right tokens, and visible legal/consent UI mixes English and Russian.
findings.suggestedFix: Translate the entire gate and consent experience consistently and migrate layout rules to logical inline/block properties.

findings.summary: Tracking begins before the consent choice can take effect.
findings.evidence: The interface offers an essential-only choice, but analytics and advertising trackers are already active while the consent prompt is still visible, so the stated choice does not precede collection.
findings.suggestedFix: Default non-essential collection to off and activate vendors only after an affirmative, granular consent choice.

findings.summary: Search disables assistance and lacks a persistent label.
findings.evidence: The visible search input has autocomplete=off and no associated label, reducing browser assistance and clarity.
findings.suggestedFix: Give search a programmatic label and permit appropriate autocomplete/search-history assistance unless there is a documented privacy reason not to.

findings.summary: Most images lack responsive modern delivery.
findings.evidence: Of 37 images, 33 lack srcset, 20 use legacy formats, and 3 lack dimensions. Image transfers totaled 1.27MB on first load.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP responsive sources with sizes/srcset, intrinsic dimensions, and appropriately sized placeholders.

findings.summary: The first load performs substantial work unrelated to immediate content.
findings.evidence: The page performs 172 requests, including 101 third-party requests, while Lighthouse estimates 288KiB unused JavaScript and 74KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused bundles, delay non-essential vendors, batch analytics, and avoid below-fold ad work until needed.

findings.summary: Third-party cost is disproportionate on the first view.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 2.26MB and 101 requests, including 31 TrafficJunky requests and multiple Google analytics/tag requests, before primary interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request and byte budget, load ads only near view after consent, and consolidate analytics.

taskList.title: Repair mobile age-gate reflow, zoom, targets, and focus
Gate analytics and advertising behind consent and reduce third-party load
Cut LCP and network cost by prioritizing critical content and deferring ads
Fix route preservation, 404 behavior, and recovery states
Add unique metadata, truthful crawler controls, canonicals, and structured data
Add CSP, nosniff, privacy policies, and safe cookie attributes
Replace custom overlays with native semantic primitives
Fix accessible names, document structure, and input labeling
Remove console errors, deprecated APIs, BFCache blockers, and unused bundles
Modernize responsive images and component layout
